children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old. I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! And one more important question: **Are you responsible for Alex? This usually means either you live with Alex, or you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them - for example on food, clothes or pocket money.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for Alex - they live with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! And just to confirm: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, there's a bit of a situation there. Alex's other parent and I are both responsible for them, but we can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that situation. I understand you and Alex's other parent are both responsible for Alex but cannot agree on who should claim.

According to the rules, if two people are responsible for the same child and cannot agree who will claim Child Benefit, HMRC (HM Revenue and Customs) will decide who will get it.

Let me ask: **Has either you or Alex's other parent already submitted a claim for Child Benefit for Alex, or is HMRC already involved in making this decision?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us has submitted a claim yet. We wanted to understand the eligibility first before sorting out who should actually claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's helpful to know.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Does Alex have any circumstances that might affect eligibility, such as:**
- Being in hospital or care for an extended period?
- Living with someone else (other than you or the other parent)?
- Working 24 hours or more per week?
- Receiving certain benefits in their own right?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply. Alex lives with me full-time, isn't in hospital or care, doesn't work, and doesn't receive any benefits in their own right. They're just a regular 8-year-old going to school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Eligibility Assessment Complete

**Good news!** You are **eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

### Summary:
- ✅ Alex is 8 years old (under the age limit of 16)
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ You are responsible for Alex, who lives with you
- ✅ No special circumstances apply that would affect eligibility
- ✅ No one is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

### Important Information About Your Situation:

Since you mentioned that you and Alex's other parent cannot agree on who should claim, here's what you should know:

- **Only one person can receive Child Benefit for Alex**
- You are eligible to make a claim
- If both you and the other parent submit claims, HMRC will decide who receives the Child Benefit

**Next Steps:**
1. You and the other parent should try to reach an agreement about who will claim
2. If you cannot agree, either of you can submit a claim, and HMRC will make the decision
3. You can proceed with making your claim for Child Benefit

**Additional Note:** If either you or your partner has an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, so keep that in mind when deciding.

If you have any other questions about the claim process or your situation, please feel free to ask!
